title: The Distant Signal
premise: Astrid Quintana smuggles memories in data-cores through the orbital customs ring above Meridian Colony, a man who has spent ten years keeping everyone at arm's length. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a burning settlement, a nameless dead woman, a signal from the dark — Astrid recognizes it as a memory he once carried and sold. The dream is a fragment of the Kestrel Landing massacre, an event Earth's archives insist never happened, erased to protect the treaty that keeps Meridian fed. Racing the countdown of Earth's final transmission loop before the relay goes permanently dark, Astrid assembles a found family of outcasts — a customs officer who betrays her oath, a child who dreams too clearly, and the ghost of the woman in the memory — to prove the massacre happened. In the end, they broadcast the truth on the last open channel; Earth cuts them off forever, but Meridian chooses exile together over comfortable lies, and Astrid finally lets himself belong.
about_author: Felix Vane is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent six years maintaining deep-space relay stations in the South Pacific before turning to fiction. He writes about people who live at the edge of signals, where every message received might be the last.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Astrid runs a memory-core shipment past customs using a forged grief-license, narrating his own careful isolation and the rules that keep him alive. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — we see a man who has made solitude into craft.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Dreamed Loudly
chapters.summary: Customs officer Sefa Ili catches Astrid's cargo but lets him go after her niece Mara describes a dream no child should have: fire, snow of ash, a woman singing. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: unease — duty beginning to crack against something inexplicable.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Astrid carries a sealed memory-core for a client who dies before retrieval, leaving him holding a horror he never opened. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: guilt — the origin of his rule never to look inside what he carries.

chapters.title: Every Child on Meridian
chapters.summary: The shared dream spreads through the colony's schools; parents panic, officials blame a contaminated entertainment feed. Mara seeks out Astrid because the woman in her dream wears his coat. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: eerie wonder tipping into fear.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Sefa queries Earth's records for Kestrel Landing and finds nothing — not denial, but absence, a surgically deleted settlement. Her report is auto-flagged and her clearance quietly reduced. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting; the first cost of asking questions.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Astrid's old fixer, Oyelaran, surfaces demanding the core Astrid has carried for ten years — and reveals others are hunting it as the children's dreams make it valuable again. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: hunted; his anonymity dies.

chapters.title: Three Strangers, One Core
chapters.summary: Astrid, Sefa, and Mara form an uneasy alliance in a dockside noodle bar; Astrid almost opens the core and cannot. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: reluctant connection — found family taking its first awkward shape.

chapters.title: The Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: They learn Earth's last scheduled transmission loop ends in nineteen days, after which the relay goes dark for a decade-long realignment — a hard deadline for broadcasting any proof. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: ticking clock installed; hope with a fuse.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: Mara teaches Astrid to enter the shared dream via a jury-rigged neural bridge; inside, the burning settlement is detailed enough to be evidence, not imagination. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: intimacy and terror — the dream knows Astrid's name.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Price
chapters.summary: Oyelaran offers the chain of custody proving the core's origin — in exchange for Astrid surrendering it unopened and walking away. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: temptation; survival offered at the price of truth.

chapters.title: Kestrel Landing, Burning
chapters.summary: Astrid finally opens the core: full sensory record of the massacre — colonists gassed to preserve treaty secrecy, the singing woman dying last. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: devastation; his decade of willful blindness collapses.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sang
chapters.summary: In the dream, the dead woman — Dr. Imke Voss, the massacre's only recorder — guides Mara to where she hid a second copy in the colony's foundations. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose; the dead recruit the living.

chapters.title: Customs House Raid
chapters.summary: Earth's liaison agents raid customs looking for the core; Sefa burns her career covering their escape and is marked a traitor. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: sacrifice — duty inverted, loyalty redirected to people instead of protocol.

chapters.title: Under the Foundations
chapters.summary: Digging beneath the original habitat ring, they find Voss's cache — physical crystal, uncorruptible, undeniable — but Oyelaran's mercenaries ambush them. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: triumph ambushed; the proof nearly lost.

chapters.title: Mara Taken
chapters.summary: The mercenaries take Mara and the cache; Oyelaran reveals he was the client who ordered the original smuggling run — erasure has been managed all along. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: despair and rage; the found family tested at its weakest point.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Last Run
chapters.summary: Astrid plans an impossible run: board Oyelaran's ship in transit using the one route customs can't watch — the one that killed his first partner. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: resolve; the loner choosing risk for someone else.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Astrid and Sefa take the ship; Sefa takes a wound shielding him; Astrid confronts Oyelaran, who argues the lie keeps forty thousand people fed. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: moral climax — comfort versus truth given its strongest voice.

chapters.title: What We Choose to Carry
chapters.summary: Astrid spares Oyelaran but seizes the cache; Mara, rescued, tells him the dream changed — the woman is singing a farewell now. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; the dead letting go.

chapters.title: Nineteen Hours
chapters.summary: With the loop ending, they must seize the relay itself; Sefa calls in every favor, and dockworkers, teachers, and smugglers — Meridian's invisible family — mobilize. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: solidarity; the colony choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Last Open Channel
chapters.summary: Climax: they broadcast Voss's full record as Earth attempts a jamming override; Astrid speaks the names of the dead into the loop's final minutes. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth spoken at maximum volume against absolute silence.

chapters.title: Exile, Together
chapters.summary: Earth cuts Meridian off permanently; panic gives way to a strange liberation as the colony turns inward to survive on its own terms. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: mourning and rebirth entwined.

chapters.title: The Distant Signal
chapters.summary: Months later, Astrid opens a legal memory-shop, Mara apprenticing beside him; on quiet nights the children still dream, but now of a city being built. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: belonging — the man who carried ghosts finally sets them down among friends.
